name: Parsley
grown_as: A biennial herb grown as an annual for its leaves. Two common forms: flat-leaved (French or Italian) and curly (moss-curled). They look very different. ⚠️ CHECK which William grows; drawn as flat-leaved.
habit: First year a tidy mound of upright leaves on long stalks, 20 to 35 cm high. Second year a branched, ridged flowering stem 60 to 100 cm.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette from the crown; alternate on the flowering stem
leaf.type: Compound, two or three times pinnate
leaf.leaflets: Flat-leaved: leaflets wedge-shaped to diamond-shaped, 1 to 3 cm, cut into three lobes. Curly: the leaflets tightly crisped and curled into a moss-like ruff.
leaf.outline: Triangular overall, 10 to 20 cm long without the stalk
leaf.base: Leaflets narrowing to a wedge base
leaf.margin: Sharp forward-pointing teeth on the upper outer edges of each lobe; the wedge base untoothed
leaf.surface: Flat-leaved: smooth, hairless and glossy. Curly: crimped and dense.
leaf.stalk: Long (10 to 20 cm), upright, grooved, with a short sheath at the base

flower.form: Flat-topped compound umbels of tiny flowers
flower.petals: Five tiny petals per flower, tips turned in
flower.behind: One to three small bracts under the umbel; five to eight thin bracteoles under each small umbel
flower.carried: At the top of the second-year stem and its branches, facing up; 8 to 20 rays
flower.season: June to August of the second year

fruit: Small egg-shaped seeds 2 to 3 mm in pairs, with fine pale ribs, grey-brown when ripe
seedling: Two narrow oblong seed leaves about 1 to 2 cm; the first true leaf rounded and three-lobed with teeth
winter: Usually keeps a small rosette of green leaves through winter, then flowers the next year

leaf: leaf divided twice or more into wedge-shaped three-lobed leaflets
sharp teeth on the outer edges, none at the base
bloom: small bracts and thin bracteoles under the umbels
seedling: a first true leaf rounded and three-lobed
young: a small rosette of divided leaves on long upright stalks
crop: a full mound of glossy dark green divided leaves on long stalks
flower: a tall branched stem with flat yellow-green umbels
seedhead: umbels of small ribbed seeds on stiff rays

look_alikes: Fool's parsley (Aethusa cynapium, poisonous) has white flowers and long hanging bracteoles on the outer side of each small umbel. Coriander leaves are softer and rounder with a different smell. Celery leaves are once pinnate with broader leaflets and fleshy stalks.
